metadata.context_method: Oracle context around a deterministic gold class; no retrieved or shuffled conditions.
metadata.oracle_centre_policy: deepest graph-minimal annotated class, class ID tie-break; all gold types retained for scoring

prompt:
List valid entity-type labels, most specific first, then broader valid types. Use concise labels, not entity names or descriptions. Include only evidence-supported types; do not repeat labels or pad the list.

The context surrounds an omitted target type; it is evidence, not answer options. Parents are broader, and siblings share a parent. Infer the type using the description and these relations. Copy a neighbour only if valid for this entity. Siblings need not be disjoint.

Briefly use parents to explain scope, compare sibling alternatives, and reject unsupported specificity. Justify the final specific-to-broad order using the description and taxonomy evidence.

Return JSON only in exactly this form:
{"explanation": "taxonomy-grounded explanation", "types": ["type 1", "type 2", "..."]}

Example:

Entity: Rod Fergusson
Description: Canadian video game producer

Taxonomy context:
- Direct parent classes: producer
- Sibling classes: creative producer, co-producer, line producer
- Direct child classes: None

Correct response:
{"explanation": "The description \"Canadian video game producer\" supports video game producer as the most specific type. In the taxonomy, its direct parent is producer, which constrains the broader semantic category. The sibling classes are nearby alternatives, but classes such as creative producer, co-producer, line producer are not as well supported by the description. The listed child context is None; a child should be selected only if the description independently supports that narrower meaning. The remaining returned types are broader valid classes ranked in decreasing specificity.", "types": ["video game producer", "producer", "media professional", "professional", "worker", "person", "person or organization", "corporate body", "object", "entity"]}

Now classify:

Entity: Kalpathy Balakrishnan
Description: musician

Taxonomy context:
- Direct parent classes: instrumentalist
- Sibling classes: clavichordist, keyboardist, double-bassist

Answer:
response: {"explanation": "The description \"musician\" supports instrumentalist as the most specific type. In the taxonomy, its direct parent is instrumentalist, which constrains the broader semantic category. The siblings are nearby alternatives related to specific instruments, but classes such as clavichordist, keyboardist, double-bassist are interpreted as characteristic rather than representative examples. Since musician may imply singing or vocal performance, but there are no child classes, vocal instrument-specific classes cannot be ruled out by lack of narrower specification. However, the description may still be more generally, it implies performing (especially as part of a band or musical group) on an instrument - see musician definition [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Musician][https://oxforddictionaries.com/definition/musician]. This is supported by evidence of family relations in broader types from WordNet which validates the placement of more general types from parent and sibling taxa. These taxonomy-grounded relations inform the general family listing up the range from very specific and highly related through increasingly broader relationships.", "types": ["musician", "instrumentalist", "performer", "entertainer", "person", "person or organization", "corporate body", "object", "entity"]}
explanation: The description "musician" supports instrumentalist as the most specific type. In the taxonomy, its direct parent is instrumentalist, which constrains the broader semantic category. The siblings are nearby alternatives related to specific instruments, but classes such as clavichordist, keyboardist, double-bassist are interpreted as characteristic rather than representative examples. Since musician may imply singing or vocal performance, but there are no child classes, vocal instrument-specific classes cannot be ruled out by lack of narrower specification. However, the description may still be more generally, it implies performing (especially as part of a band or musical group) on an instrument - see musician definition [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Musician][https://oxforddictionaries.com/definition/musician]. This is supported by evidence of family relations in broader types from WordNet which validates the placement of more general types from parent and sibling taxa. These taxonomy-grounded relations inform the general family listing up the range from very specific and highly related through increasingly broader relationships.
